messages:
alex: @maria — heads up, customer jane@acme is seeing intermittent 429s. They report it started after they put a small proxy in front of our API to rotate keys for per-request routing. They say no single key looks over its dashboard quota, but the app gets bursts of 429s under load.

customer-jane: hit 429s on stage when load hits ~300 rps. We rotate through 4 keys from the proxy. Dashboard for each key shows ~low usage; org billing shows a big jump around the time of the bursts but we can't tell which level is tripping. Response headers below from one of the 429s: 

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: org=200000;project=20000;key=5000;ip=1000
x-rate-limit-remaining: key=0;ip=998
x-rate-limit-reset: 1852509900
Retry-After: 25
X-Request-Id: req_0a7f1b

customer-jane: repro steps:
1) proxy receives burst, rotates key each request
2) parallel clients ~300 rps for 30s
3) ~5-10% of requests start getting 429s, then spikes to ~30%

maria: thanks — a few quick asks: can you paste the exact Authorization header you rotate (mask key), the proxy IP range, and whether the rotation is round-robin or hashed per-user? also we need the X-Request-Id from some 429 responses.

customer-jane: auth header is Authorization: Bearer sk_proj_XXXX (we rotate 4 keys). Rotation is round-robin by request. Proxy IPs are a small pool behind NAT (3 egress IPs). sample X-Request-Id: req_0a7f1b, req_0a7f2c.

sachin: initial theory: they're hitting an org-level aggregated quota or an IP-based burst limit. rotating keys will avoid per-key soft limits but not org-level or ip-based caps. the headers showing org=200000 and key=5000 imply multi-level scoping. note x-rate-limit-remaining shows key=0 so that particular key got exhausted. but ip remaining is high, which suggests keys exhausted faster. however the billing spike reported could be org aggregation catching up once retries/backoffs happen.

patrick: also check whether the proxy is multiplexing connections poorly — lots of short-lived TCP connections prevents keep-alive and increases per-request overhead which can trigger some internal burst mitigation. can they run a repro with a single persistent connection and see if 429s drop?

alex: good point. customer, can you run two quick repros?

1) single key, persistent connection (keep-alive) at 300 rps for 30s
2) 4-key rotation, same load

Add `--header "Connection: keep-alive"` to curl. Example:

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_proj_XXXX" -H "Connection: keep-alive" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' &
  sleep 0.003
done
wait
```

maria: also ask them to capture the raw response headers for first 20 429s. the presence/absence of `x-rate-limit-scope` or similar fields will tell us whether the enforcement was keyed to org/project/ip.

ops-bot: Rate limit alert: org org_acme (org_abc) exceeded soft burst threshold at 2026-07-03T12:45:03Z — aggregated qps 4.2k over 1m. Event id rl_evt_4932.

sachin: ops-bot event confirms a short org-level burst. rollout: because proxy rotates keys rapidly, the org sees higher aggregated concurrency than any single key's dashboard indicates. dashboards that show per-key usage can be misleading for this pattern.

maria: TL;DR patterns we should explain to customer:
- per-key quotas limit each key independently
- project quotas group keys under a project (if used)
- org quotas are aggregated across all projects/keys and will block when total throughput exceeds org limits
- IP-based heuristics can add another layer (e.g., many requests from same egress IP pool may trigger network-level throttles)

customer-jane: oh — so rotating keys doesn't buy you infinite headroom — got it. is there a recommended pattern to avoid this without increasing org quota?

alex: mitigations:
- implement exponential backoff + jitter on 429s (don't retry immediately across rotated keys)
- add jitter to rotation to avoid synchronized bursts
- reuse keys for bursts instead of rotating per-request (reduces org aggregation spike due to auth overhead)
- spread traffic across time, use a token-bucket locally to smooth bursts
- request a temporary org-level burst raise from support if this is a known onboarding spike

patrick: operational quick-checks we need from them before escalation:
- list of egress IPs (we want to confirm ip-based layer)
- sample request/response headers for 429s (X-Request-Id mandatory)
- whether their proxy terminates TLS (affects connection reuse)

maria: also an edge-case — API keys can be scoped to project or org depending on how created. if keys are org-scoped then per-key dashboards may under-report aggregated usage on project-level or vice versa. we should confirm key scope in our auth table. I'll query auth-service for sk_proj_XXXX to verify scope.

sachin: repro plan for us:
- try to reproduce in staging using a 3-ip NAT gateway and 4 rotating keys (simulate their rotation)
- compare single-key burst vs key-rotation burst, capture rps, TCP connections, keep-alive metrics
- check rate-limit enforcement logs for scope (we log enforcement reason as: reason=(org_quota|project_quota|key_quota|ip_burst) with request id)

maria: please escalate to quota team if auth-service returns key_scope=project but enforcement shows org_quota. I'll take point on auth lookup. sachin, can you run the staging repro and paste the enforcement logs? I'll update the customer after we have concrete evidence.

sachin: on it. I will:
- deploy a small repro in staging at 3pm PST
- run both patterns for 5 minutes each
- paste logs and the exact enforcement lines

alex: customer-facing note I'm going to send after we have logs: "Thanks for the repro steps — we've reproduced the burst behavior in staging. The 429s come from org-level aggregation combined with short TCP connections from the proxy. Recommended short-term: add jitter + backoff, reuse connections; we can also request a temporary org burst increase while you smooth traffic. We'll follow up with exact enforcement lines. — Alex (Support)"

customer-jane: thank you — will add the header captures and egress IPs now.

patrick: one more edge-case to watch: if their proxy tampers with Authorization headers (e.g., strips/rewrites) we might be seeing mixed identity attribution which could complicate billing/quotas. ask them to confirm raw outgoing header content from the proxy.

maria: noted. assigning owners: maria -> auth lookup & routing rules check, sachin -> staging repro & enforcement logs, alex -> customer comms & temporary quota request. patrick -> proxy connection guidance.

sachin: logging snippet we'll look for in enforcement logs (example):
```
[2026-07-03T12:45:03Z] req=req_0a7f1b enforcement=org_quota scope=org org_id=org_acme used=202550 limit=200000 reason=burst
```

maria: if we see enforcement=ip_burst with scope=ip then suggest they get a larger egress CIDR or use multiple egress pools.

alex: closing note — we'll follow up in this thread after staging runs. thanks team. :thumbsup:
